info.title: YOB Storefront & Auth API — frontend contract
info.description:
Frappe RPC API. Every response is wrapped by Frappe in an outer `message` object; inside is the YOB envelope (`data` plus optional `notice`/`meta` on success, `errors[]` on failure). There is no `success` boolean: branch on HTTP status, then `errors[0].code`.

Authenticated storefront endpoints need the HttpOnly `sid` cookie and, for non-GET, `X-Frappe-CSRF-Token`.

The three payment endpoints are PUBLIC. `/payment/<token>` requires NO storefront session: `get_checkout_data` and `process_payment` are authorized by the checkout token, and `verify_payment` by Razorpay's HMAC signature. Do not place them behind a session guard.

See FRONTEND-CONTRACT.md for prose that this document cannot fully express.

OrderListRow.description: One row of `order.get_orders`. Exactly these six fields.

currency.description: the order's OWN stored currency -- never infer from environment configuration

discount_amount.description: (price_list_rate - rate) * qty, computed by the API

OrderPaymentLog.description: Razorpay Payment Log row, newest first. Empty for an unpaid or Pay Later order.

payment_method.description: the PROVIDER's method string ("netbanking", "card", ...). NOT the YOB Payment Method name sent to process_payment.

contact_email.description: from the Sales Order's stored field, NOT the Contact master. Frequently null on storefront orders.

billing_address_name.description: IDENTIFIER ONLY -- the linked Address master, which points at CURRENT data and may have been edited or deleted. Never render as the order's address.

billing_address_display.description: HISTORICAL. Plain text with real newlines -- never HTML, do not use [innerHTML]. Taken from the order's immutable order-time snapshot, so editing the Address master does not change a past order. `string | null` in every branch, never an object.

taxes.description: RAW ERPNext `Sales Taxes and Charges` child rows, passed through unprojected. Columns are ERPNext's and are NOT pinned by this contract; no real order observed so far has a tax row. Display only.

VariantAttribute.description: One selectable attribute, in the TEMPLATE's own order.

numeric.description: 1 when ERPNext defines this attribute as numeric. The values below are still the ones that OCCUR; no range is expanded.

values.description: ONLY values occurring in salable variants, already in the merchant's own order (S, M, L). Do not sort. Not a grid: see `variants[]`.

VariantCombination.description: One ACTUAL salable variant. The complete list of what can be bought.

VariantFamily.description: A variant FAMILY (Item Template). Never priced and never purchasable: ERPNext refuses an Item Price on a template. Told apart from a product by `is_template = 1`.

name.description: the TEMPLATE item code; pass it as `template` to resolve_variant

custom_slug.description: the public URL segment; belongs to the family, never to a variant

is_purchasable.description: 0 always. Adding this code to the cart answers item_is_template.

variants.description: THE authority on valid combinations. A pair absent here does not exist: render it disabled, never resolve it.

ProductDetail.description: The shared product-detail serializer. Returned by get_item for a simple Item and by resolve_variant for a resolved variant, so one DTO serves both. Every monetary and unit value comes from ERPNext's own pricing of a temporary Sales Order.

name.description: the ACTUAL item code; the only value to send to add_to_cart

custom_slug.description: null for a variant: variants have no public URL

qty.description: the quantity this preview was priced for

variant_of.description: the family, when this is a variant

selected.description: the variant's STORED attribute map, read from ERPNext -- not echoed from the request. null for a simple Item.

uom.description: the selling unit ERPNext resolved; SHOW IT beside the quantity

stock_uom.description: the unit stock is counted in

stock_qty.description: qty x conversion_factor, derived by ERPNext

actual_qty.description: in `stock_uom`, NEVER converted. null = does not apply or unknown; 0 = none in stock.

pricing.description: the raw pricing block; prefer the flattened fields above

ListingCard.description: One catalogue card. ONE card per simple Item and ONE per variant family -- never one per variant. `price_state` discriminates.

price_state.description: `select_options` = a family; every monetary field below is null. Never invent a price -- ERPNext cannot price a template.

ProductSuggestion.description:
One public product in the header typeahead. Deliberately minimal: enough to draw a dropdown row and open the product page, and **nothing monetary**.

There is no rate, discount, tax, UOM, conversion factor, stock, warehouse or pricing rule here, and there will not be -- the product page is authoritative once the buyer clicks, and a price in a dropdown is a second place for money to be wrong. Do not treat this as a small `ListingCard`; it is a different contract for a different job.

item_name.description: What to show in the dropdown row.

slug.description: The public slug. Navigate to the product page with it; every suggestion has one, because a product without a public URL is never suggested.

image.description: Relative path as stored (`/files/...`), the same convention `ListingCard` uses, or null. Use your existing media helper unchanged.

is_template.description: True for a variant FAMILY, which opens an options page rather than a directly buyable product. Generated variants are never suggested on their own.

items.description: At most 8, ordered by product name. Empty when the search is shorter than 3 characters, which is not an error.

ItemDetailResponse.description: get_item answers ONE of two modes; discriminate on `data.is_template`.

Destination.description: Where a navigation item or clickable block goes. `null` means not clickable OR that the target is no longer publishable -- render both the same way. Never contains database identity.

target.description: public slug of the target; null for implied routes

href.description: ready-made route where one exists. **always null for `storefront_page`** -- the SPA route is `/pages/:slug`, built from `target` on the client.

children.description: one level only: a root Group carries leaves, and a leaf's `children` is always []. Recursive by schema, never by data -- a grandchild cannot be stored.

items.description: no counts: a truthful count needs the full eligibility pipeline per value

BannerCarouselSlide.description: One slide of a `banner_carousel` block. Slides arrive in the merchant's own row order -- render them in the order given and do not re-sort. Every field except the images is optional content, and `destination` is null when the slide is not clickable OR its target is no longer publishable.

desktop_image.description: relative path as stored, e.g. `/files/hero.png` -- the catalogue convention, never an absolute URL. Required in Desk, so non-null in practice; the projection still permits null and a client must not crash on it.

mobile_image.description: optional narrow-viewport art; fall back to `desktop_image` when null

title.description: merchant caption; absent as often as not

PromoCard.description: One card of a `promo_grid` block. Structurally identical to `BannerCarouselSlide` -- both are the same merchant-authored media row with a shared destination -- but they are separate schemas because they are separate stored types and may diverge. Cards arrive in the merchant's own row order; do not re-sort. A promo card is merchandising art, NOT an ERPNext Pricing Rule: nothing here discounts anything.

desktop_image.description: relative path as stored, e.g. `/files/hero.png` -- the catalogue convention, never an absolute URL. Required in Desk, so non-null in practice; the projection still permits null and a client must not crash on it.

mobile_image.description: optional narrow-viewport art; fall back to `desktop_image` when null

title.description: merchant caption; absent as often as not

SectionStyle.description:
The semantic band a block sits in. Set per PLACEMENT, never on the reusable Block, so the same Block can be `muted` on a page and `dark` on a route. **Semantic only.** The backend does not define colour, padding, text colour, breakpoints, the fixed content width or the full-bleed behaviour -- the SPA maps each key to source-controlled styling. It is not a class name and never arbitrary CSS. The intended shape is a full-width section wrapping a fixed-width container: `
...block...
` `default` means the ordinary page background. Rows written before this field existed project as `default`, so it is always present.

ContentWidth.description:
Whether the block itself is held inside the fixed content container or spans the full width of its section. Set per PLACEMENT, never on the reusable Block, so the same hero Banner can run full width on one route and contained on a page. ``` contained full_width
...block... ...block...
``` **Horizontal containment ONLY.** It does not control the section background or style (`section_style` does), vertical spacing, block or image height, which responsive image is chosen, or any margin/padding value -- those stay in source-controlled CSS. Independent of `section_style`: every combination is valid, and neither is derived from the other. Valid for ALL block types, not only banners. `contained` is what every placement did before this field existed, and rows predating it project as `contained`, so it is always present.

ContentBlock.description:
Discriminated by `type`. Each block carries ONLY its own type's fields -- never infer the kind from which nullable fields are set. `type`, `block_name`, `section_style` and `content_width` are present on every block. The last two are the PLACEMENT's presentation -- from the Page Block row or the Content Placement, never from the reusable Block -- so one Block can be `muted`+`contained` in one location and `default`+`full_width` in another. They are independent of each other; every other property below names the block types that actually carry it, and a client must not read a property outside those types.

Per type, the fields the runtime always emits:
* `image_banner` -- desktop_image, mobile_image, alt_text, desktop_height_px, mobile_height_px, destination
* `rich_text` -- title, html, text_alignment
* `banner_carousel` -- auto_play, interval_ms, desktop_height_px, mobile_height_px, slides
* `promo_grid` -- cards_per_row, desktop_height_px, mobile_height_px, cards
* `product_grid` -- card_type, item_limit, category, items (NO height fields: a grid is sized by its cards, not by a merchant-set pixel height)

desktop_image.description: `image_banner` only. Relative path as stored, e.g. `/files/hero.png` -- the catalogue convention, never an absolute URL.

mobile_image.description: `image_banner` only. Fall back to `desktop_image` when null.

desktop_height_px.description: `image_banner`, `banner_carousel` and `promo_grid`. The merchant's chosen media height in CSS pixels; null means unset, so use your own default rather than collapsing to zero. Absent entirely on `rich_text` and `product_grid`.

mobile_height_px.description: `image_banner`, `banner_carousel` and `promo_grid`. The merchant's chosen media height in CSS pixels; null means unset, so use your own default rather than collapsing to zero. Absent entirely on `rich_text` and `product_grid`.

destination.description: `image_banner` only. Slides and cards carry their own.

title.description: `rich_text` only -- the block heading. Slides and promo cards have their own `title`.

html.description: `rich_text` only. Sanitised server-side on save; still render through your own trusted-HTML policy -- this is the first boundary, not the only one.

interval_ms.description: `banner_carousel` only. Null means unset -- choose your own interval.

slides.description: `banner_carousel` only. In the merchant's row order; do not re-sort.

cards_per_row.description: `promo_grid` only. A layout hint of 1, 2 or 3; null means unset.

cards.description: `promo_grid` only. In the merchant's row order; do not re-sort.

item_limit.description: `product_grid` only. The merchant's configured cap, 1..12. `items` may be SHORTER when the category holds fewer eligible products; it is never longer.

category.description: `product_grid` only. The category's public slug, or null when the configured category became unusable (disabled, or turned into a group) -- `items` is then empty and NEVER a fallback listing.

items.description: `product_grid` only. The SAME ListingCard the catalogue returns, produced by the same service: customer-priced, family cards carry `price_state: select_options` with every money field null.

ContentSlot.description: One application-owned position on a route, with the merchant content placed in it. `blocks` is often empty and that is normal, not an error: EVERY slot the route declares is returned so a client can render `slots` without first checking whether a key exists.

key.description: Slot key, unique WITHIN its route. The same key may appear on more than one route (`above_listing` is on both `catalog` and `category`); it is the (route, slot) PAIR that identifies a position.

blocks.description: In the merchant's order (`sequence`, then a stable tie-break). The IDENTICAL ContentBlock union `cms.get_page` returns -- one projector serves both, so a renderer written for pages needs no changes.

slots.description: Every slot the route declares, in render order.

example._comment: `data` is an empty object. Re-read get_addresses; the list cache is already invalidated server-side.

value._comment: HTTP 409. A Cart, a historical Sales Order, or the Customer default still references this address. It still EXISTS -- keep it in the list. Nothing is detached automatically, so this is not retryable. The referring document is deliberately not named.

errors.detail: This address is currently in use and can't be deleted.

post.description:
**AUTHENTICATED STOREFRONT**

Deletion is CONDITIONAL. Frappe refuses to delete a record another document still references.

- 200 -> deleted (`data` is `{}`)
- 404 `address_not_found` -> unknown, or not this customer's. Terminal.
- 409 `address_in_use` -> still referenced by a Cart, a historical Sales Order, or the Customer's default address. The record STILL EXISTS -- keep it in the list.

Nothing is detached automatically, so a 409 is NOT retryable: the user must change the selection first. The response carries only the code and a plain sentence; the referring document is deliberately not named.

DO NOT auto-retry a delete whose response was lost: the retry answers 404 and turns a success into an apparent error. Re-read the list instead.

value._comment: HTTP 409, the Contact mirror of delete-address-in-use-409. Previously this escaped as a raw Frappe LinkExistsError at HTTP 417 with Desk HTML in _server_messages.

errors.detail: This contact is currently in use and can't be deleted.

validation_failed.summary: 422 -- a required field was cleared, or a value rejected

value._comment: Sent { name, city: "" } -- an explicit clear of a REQUIRED field. The record is untouched. `field` names what to fix; previously this was a generic 500 with no field.

post.description:
**AUTHENTICATED STOREFRONT**

**PARTIAL UPDATE.** Send `name` plus only the fields you are editing.

Semantics are keyed on request PRESENCE, not truthiness:
- omitted -> UNCHANGED (the stored value is preserved)
- supplied value -> validated and applied
- explicit empty string on an optional field -> CLEARED
- invalid value -> `validation_failed` (422), record untouched

DO NOT resend untouched optional fields to preserve them. That was a workaround for a real bug (this endpoint used to assign every field unconditionally and blanked whatever was omitted) and it is now HARMFUL: an explicit empty value is a deliberate clear.

Idempotent -- the same payload applied twice converges. `name` identifies the record and is not editable; changing the title renames nothing, so links from historical documents stay stable.

example._comment: email/phone are read back from the SAVED record. They previously echoed the request, so an omitted email reported null while the contact still had one.

post.description:
**AUTHENTICATED STOREFRONT**

**qty is a DELTA added to any existing line for this item_code -- it does NOT replace it. Line qty 2 + add qty 5 = 7, on ONE row. A quantity stepper must send the difference. NOT idempotent: a retry or double-submit adds twice. There is no absolute set-quantity endpoint.**

Takes `item_code` + `qty` and NOTHING else. After resolving a variant, send `data.name` from `resolve_variant` as `item_code`. UOM, warehouse, conversion factor, price list and rate are server-derived and are not accepted from a client.

The SKU is revalidated server-side before anything is read or written:

* `item_is_template` (422) -- the code is a variant FAMILY; families are never purchasable.
* `item_not_purchasable` (422) -- disabled, not a sales item, past end of life, or an orphaned variant.
* `item_not_found` (404) -- no such Item.
* `cart_item_uom_changed` (409) -- the selling unit of an existing line moved.

`qty` is a DELTA added to any existing line for that SKU.

qty.description: qty is a DELTA added to any existing line for this item_code -- it does NOT replace it. Line qty 2 + add qty 5 = 7, on ONE row. A quantity stepper must send the difference. NOT idempotent: a retry or double-submit adds twice. There is no absolute set-quantity endpoint. Fractional values accepted.

get.description:
**AUTHENTICATED STOREFRONT**

One PUBLIC product page. A slug addresses a **simple Item** or a **variant FAMILY** (Item Template) -- never an individual variant: variants have no public URL and are reached by resolving attributes on the family page.

TWO RESPONSE MODES, discriminated by `data.is_template`:

* `is_template = 0` -- a purchasable product; the shared product-detail payload.
* `is_template = 1` -- a family; `attributes[]` + `variants[]` and **no price at all**, because ERPNext refuses an Item Price on a template.

Valid combinations come ONLY from `variants[]`, which lists actual salable variants. Attribute values are global in ERPNext, so a cross-product of `attributes[].values` invents combinations nobody can buy -- render those disabled.

A `Manufacturer`-based family answers `variant_family_unsupported` (422).

get.description:
**AUTHENTICATED STOREFRONT**

`order_id` is REQUIRED. Omitting it answers 422 `validation_failed` with `field: "order_id"` -- it is not treated as "list all".

Scoped to the authenticated Customer server-side. Another customer's order and a non-existent order both answer 404 `order_not_found`, identically, so the response cannot be used to probe for other customers' orders.

**Addresses are historical snapshots.** `billing_address_display` and `shipping_address_display` are `string | null` PLAIN TEXT (real newlines, never HTML) taken from the order's immutable order-time snapshot -- editing the Address master does not change a past order. `billing_address_name` / `shipping_address_name` are identifiers only and point at the CURRENT master. The former `billing_address` / `shipping_address` OBJECTS were removed: they read the master live and made order history mutable.

`contact_*` likewise come from the order's stored fields, not the Contact master, and are frequently null.

**AUTHENTICATED STOREFRONT**

**Takes no parameters.** No filter, search, date range, page or limit exists; the whole list is returned every time.

**Ordered by `creation` DESCENDING -- newest order first.** The server sorts; render the array as received and do not re-sort client-side. The sort key is the creation timestamp, NOT `transaction_date`: same-day orders share a `transaction_date`, and `creation` is not in the response, so a client sort cannot reproduce the correct order.

Each row carries the Sales Order's OWN stored `currency`. Never infer order-list currency from environment configuration.

get.description: **AUTHENTICATED STOREFRONT**

**AUTHENTICATED STOREFRONT**

Turns a COMPLETE attribute selection into the actual ERPNext variant and prices it. The server resolves the SKU through ERPNext's own `find_variant` and revalidates that it is salable; a client must never build an item code itself.

`attributes` is a JSON object of EVERY attribute the family defines, sent as a query parameter (URL-encoded JSON string). A mapping is also accepted for non-browser callers.

Answers the shared product-detail payload, identical to `get_item` for a simple Item, plus `variant_of` and `selected`. `selected` is read from the variant's stored attribute rows -- never echoed from the request.

No server state is kept for a partial selection: re-anchoring, clearing and re-choosing are entirely a client concern.

parameters.name: template
parameters.description: the TEMPLATE item code, i.e. `data.name` from the family page

parameters.name: attributes
parameters.description: JSON object; every attribute of the family must be present

parameters.name: qty
parameters.description: quantity to price the preview for; pricing is quantity-dependent

422.description: `variant_attributes_required` -- not every attribute was chosen. `variant_not_available` -- that combination has no salable variant; it is never resolved to a neighbour.

parameters.name: scope_type
parameters.description: only `category` is implemented; anything else answers unsupported_scope

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: matched against the product name OR its item code; words are ANDed, and each word may be satisfied by either column

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: must be absent or empty; anything else answers unsupported_filters

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: 1..48; out of range is refused, not clamped

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: opaque keyset cursor from a previous page

parameters.name: storefront_filters
parameters.description: JSON object keyed by filter/value KEYS from `get_category_filters`. Values within one filter are OR-ed; different filters are AND-ed. A selection, never query grammar -- unknown keys are refused, not queried -- and it requires a category scope.

422.description: `storefront_filter_invalid` (malformed), `storefront_filter_unknown` (not exposed by this category), `storefront_filter_value_unknown` (not a value of that filter, or disabled), `storefront_filter_context_required` (no category scope).

get.description:
**AUTHENTICATED STOREFRONT**

ONE card per simple Item and ONE per variant FAMILY -- never one per variant. Every card carries `has_variants` and `price_state`:

* `price_state = "priced"` -- a simple Item; monetary fields populated.
* `price_state = "select_options"` -- a family; **every monetary field is null**. Render 'Select options'. No representative price is invented: ERPNext cannot price a template, and pricing every variant would make the page unbounded.

**Merchandising filters (Phase 25C).** `storefront_filters` narrows the listing before any pricing happens, so a narrower selection costs FEWER pricing calls. The normalised selection is part of the cursor binding: a cursor issued for one selection answers `cursor_invalid` if replayed against another. Value order and duplicates do not change the query. `filters` remains reserved and still answers `unsupported_filters`.

A few public products for the header typeahead. **Navigation only.**

At most **8** results, no pagination, no cursor, no facets, no category scope and no money. It is not a listing and not a search-results page: there is no results page for this feature, and Enter does nothing.

**Fewer than 3 characters answers `{"items": []}` and queries nothing.** That is not an error -- a buyer mid-word has done nothing wrong. The SPA applies the same floor; the server enforces it rather than trusting it.

**Same products as the catalogue.** Eligibility is the listing's own -- the same candidate rules (public slug, family collapse, manufacturer fail-closed, end-of-life) and the same base-price visibility rule -- so a suggestion is always something `get_items` would list. A generated variant never appears on its own; a family appears once, as the family, with `is_template: true`.

**Search matching** is the catalogue's, shared with `get_items`: each word is matched against the product NAME or its ITEM CODE, AND across words, with `%` and `_` treated as literal characters. So `hex 10` can take `hex` from the name and `10` from the code, and a code fragment such as `STO-ITEM-2026` finds products directly. Description, category, Item Group and Brand are not searchable.

Scope is **global** -- the same products answer from the cart, the account page or a product page. Authenticated like every other catalogue endpoint; the Customer comes from the session only, so a buyer is never suggested a product their own catalogue would not list.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: What the buyer typed. Trimmed; under 3 characters answers an empty list. Over 100 characters or more than 6 words answers `search_too_long`, exactly as `get_items` does.

200.description: Up to 8 suggestions, or an empty list.

422.description: `search_too_long` -- over 100 characters or more than 6 words.

get.description:
**AUTHENTICATED STOREFRONT**

One published navigation menu as an ordered tree, at most two levels. A node appears only when the menu, the item, its parent and its destination all still resolve -- a category that was disabled or a page that was unpublished drops the item instead of shipping a dead link, and a group left with no children drops too.

Destinations are normalised (see `Destination`): a semantic type plus a public slug. Database identity never appears.

4XX.description: `menu_not_found` (404) -- unknown OR disabled; the two are deliberately indistinguishable.

get.description:
**AUTHENTICATED STOREFRONT**

A published page and its ordered, discriminated blocks. Requires the storefront Customer because a page may hold Product Grids, which are priced for that buyer -- so this response is CUSTOMER-SPECIFIC and must never be cached across customers.

get.summary: Merchant content for one application route
get.description:
Every content slot of ONE application page, in a single request.

Slots are **application-owned**: Angular decides which routes exist and where a `<yob-content-slot>` sits inside each. A merchant chooses WHAT goes in a slot and in what ORDER, never where a slot is. This is not a page builder.

`blocks` is the SAME `ContentBlock` union `cms.get_page` returns, produced by the same projector -- a renderer written for pages works here unchanged.

**Customer-specific.** A slot may hold a Product Grid, which is priced through the buyer's own context, so this response must never be cached across customers.

Login, checkout, payment and the payment callback deliberately have no slots and answer `content_route_unknown`.

parameters.name: route_key
parameters.description: Which application page. Unknown values are refused, never mapped to a neighbouring route.

200.description: Every declared slot for the route, empty ones included.

get.description:
**AUTHENTICATED STOREFRONT**

Which merchandising filters to display for a category. Decided by that category's own Filter Set and nothing else: no inheritance from a parent category, no fallback to an item's admin scope, no fallback to every global filter. A category with no Filter Set answers `[]`.

Values are those actually assigned to a listing entity in the category, so a facet never offers a choice that returns nothing. **No counts** -- a truthful count would need the full eligibility pipeline per value.

Use the `key` values in `get_items?storefront_filters=...`.
